value.rationale: Nonstationary Brownian-powered harmonic traps arise directly in the 2026 motivating physical model. Determining the entire scaled thermal-position law is substantively different from knowing finite-time moments or the Gaussian-mixture identity. The theorem identifies a power-dependent phase of heavy-tail moment thresholds, a surprising exact Cauchy distribution for quadratic stiffness and an observable self-normalization that gives asymptotically environment-independent Gaussian fluctuations; all persist for fixed nonnegative baseline stiffness. These results give mathematically useful distributional information beyond moment formulas and clarify finite-time/long-time nonuniformity.
